title: UI Conventions
intro: MTG Arena is the reference for Beryl's flow, the order and timing of events, table layout and wording (AGENTS.md, UI; [Engine architecture](engine-architecture.md), K22). This page lists only what Arena does not settle: where Beryl differs on purpose, what Arena has no equivalent for, and what the recordings do not show.

The rulings were made on 2026-11-10 from an audit of 180 bug reports against the recordings in `~/arena`. Each Arena finding cites the recording moments that show it, as `<recording id> <time>`, for `just video film`.
This page is generated from `data/ui-conventions.json` (K28) by `just conventions`: edit the data, not the page. The repo lane fails when the page is stale.

sections.heading: Beryl exceptions
intro: Beryl does these and Arena does not. A bug report from the user adds, changes or removes an entry; nothing else does.

sections.heading: Settled as Arena
intro: Arena's way stands where an earlier report asked for something else, so do not restore the old behavior.

sections.heading: Not seen in Arena
intro: Built from motions and shapes Beryl already has. Arena has these, but the recordings do not show them.

sections.heading: Still open
intro: To be settled from the recordings (Project 50k, presentation track). Until then the current behavior stays.

lists.heading: Verbs
intro: Every change on the table is shown by one of these, applied to a card, an ability or a player by a step of the script the session sends (`engine/crates/beryl_protocol/src/script`, K23). The list is closed: what Arena does not show is composed from these. A verb's duration, delay, stagger and curve, and each case's, are the values below. The session reads them to time each step of the script (`beryl_protocol/src/script/timing.rs`). the client plays that timing. `just client check` checks the motion in a recording, and `data/arena-motion.json` holds Arena's measured instances (K27).

lists.heading: Effects
intro: An effect is light or a change of surface on one card or one player's life total, begun by a step of a verb as it starts, as it ends or as its blow lands and played on the client's script clock. Effects leave card placement and script timing alone. The list is closed. Each effect has one look defined under `data/client/effects/`, and a verb names the effects its steps begin. A mark says what a player may do; an effect says what just happened, and is gone.

lists.heading: Marks
intro: A mark is the only highlight a card, an ability or a player carries, in a script or in a prompt (K26). The list is closed, and each mark has one look. What a card's own state says (tapped, summoning sick, counters, attacking) is its face, not a mark.

entries.name: Phase icons
entries.rule: Twelve icons, two rows of three on each side of the life total, filled where a stop is set, the same rows for both seats.

arena.does: Arena shows one row above the action button.

entries.name: Full cards that tap
entries.rule: A permanent is its whole card and turns when it taps. Each row stands its permanents apart with a gap, and a crowded row shrinks them, to no less than three fifths of their size, before it lays one over another.

arena.does: Arena shows a crop of the art, on cards small enough that a row of them stands apart with a gap even on a crowded board (IACoyoys7w8 38:40 and 42:45).

entries.name: No question before a choice
entries.rule: Never ask a yes or no whose answer the next screen could take: open the search, chooser or payment with a way to decline.

arena.does: Arena asks "Search your library…?" first.

entries.name: Target arrows by relationship
entries.rule: Red at something an opponent controls, green at your own. This is skin, listed so nobody removes it.

arena.does: Arena draws every target arrow cyan, whoever controls either end; its one red line is an opponent's declared attack, with a red chevron under the attacker.

entries.name: Lands unstacked until seven
entries.rule: Each land is separate until its controller has seven or more; then same-named lands stack.

arena.does: Arena piles same-named lands from the second copy, a tapped pile apart from an untapped one, and a pile of four shows "x4".

entries.name: Linked exile under its host
entries.rule: A card exiled "until this leaves the battlefield" sits tucked under the permanent that exiled it.

arena.does: Arena shows no link on the table.

entries.name: Own-target warning
entries.rule: Confirm before a counter or removal spell targets the player's own spell or permanent.

entries.name: Cards put back in one screen
entries.rule: Cards a player puts from their hand on top of their library (Brainstorm, Jace, the Mind Sculptor's 0) are chosen and ordered in one screen over the shaded table: the library face down at the left, the cards put on it fanned down its face with the top card lowest and in front, and the hand fanned beside it. A click moves a card between the hand and the library, and a drag puts it at a height on the library.

arena.does: Arena has the cards picked in the hand itself, "Put two cards into your library. (ordering will be done in next step)" with Submit, then orders them in an "Order Cards" screen between Bottom and Top (AhTcvQ-lQQQ 4:52, IT6nwh6HtYk 10:35).

entries.name: A batch exile
entries.rule: Cards exiled together leave one at a time, about 0.3 s apart.

arena.does: Delve's cards gather on the graveyard, then peel off its top one by one into a vortex. Delve is the only batch exile in the recordings, all in one recording.

entries.name: A card a look puts in the graveyard
entries.rule: It appears on the graveyard at pile size once the chooser closes; it is not shown large first.

arena.does: A surveilled card lands on the graveyard as the overlay closes; kept cards close with the overlay.

entries.name: A card you may cast from your graveyard
entries.rule: While you may cast a card from your graveyard (flashback, such as Snapcaster Mage gives, escape, or a permanent that lets you), it lies at the right end of your hand's fan, after the cards really in your hand, ringed in a soft violet halo that breathes slowly, apart from the cyan outline of a card you may play. It flies from the graveyard into the fan in about half a second as it becomes castable, and back onto the graveyard when it no longer is. Cast, it flies from its place in the fan to the stack. The opponent's castable cards stay on their graveyard.

arena.does: When Past in Flames resolves, the cards in the graveyard that gained flashback leave the graveyard together and fan into the hand within about a quarter of a second, to the right of the cards already there, each wrapped in drifting white and violet smoke over the cyan outline of a card that may be played. One cast leaves the fan for the stack.

entries.name: A countered spell
entries.rule: It leaves before the spell that countered it.

arena.does: The countered spell crumbles in place under the counterspell, which stays until the debris is gone and then fades, 0.5 to 0.9 s later.

entries.name: A finished ability
entries.rule: It is removed at once, with no fade.

entries.name: A line from an ability to its source
entries.rule: It is always shown while the ability is on the stack, thin and faint as Arena draws it, and hidden during a prompt. A heavy arrow is not that line.

entries.name: Additional costs
entries.rule: A chooser that lowers the mana to pay (Delve) opens before mana taps; a sacrifice cost is chosen after the lands tap.

arena.does: Treasure Cruise's Delve chooser opens before any land taps; Natural Order's lands send their mana, then "Sacrifice a green creature." opens.

entries.name: An arrow to the pointer
entries.rule: While a target is chosen, an arrow runs from the spell or ability that asks to the mouse, thin and pale. On something that may be chosen it becomes the arrow the choice will draw, in that arrow's color and along its way, and the click draws the stage's own. It follows the pointer itself, with no lag: only the swing onto a target takes time. Nothing is drawn over a target already chosen, and a touch pulls none.

arena.does: As the prompt opens, a cyan arrow runs from the ability that asks to the creature under the cursor, and what may be chosen is outlined.

entries.name: An opponent's spell returned to hand
entries.rule: It breaks up in place on the stack over 0.5 to 1 s; it does not fly or flip toward their hand.

arena.does: Seen for Remand on the opponent's spells.

entries.name: Attacking a planeswalker
entries.rule: No prompt: an attacker defaults to the player, and the player pulls an arrow to the planeswalker.

arena.does: Attackers that can attack get a cyan outline; a clicked attacker turns gold, the opponent's life total and the planeswalker glow, and an arrow follows the cursor to the planeswalker.

entries.name: Button order
entries.rule: It follows Arena prompt by prompt; there is no blanket "default on the right".

entries.name: Cards put on the bottom after a mulligan
entries.rule: A card clicked in the hand glides down into its slot under the hand in a quarter of a second, slowing as it arrives, and the cards left in the hand close up in about a sixth of a second. A card clicked in its slot glides back up to its place in the hand the same way. Nothing jumps from one place to the other.

arena.does: Arena's card is dragged to a Library box at the left of the hand, then settles into the library in about 0.2 s, slowing as it arrives, and slips behind its top card; the hand closes up as the card leaves it. Beryl keeps its slots under the hand, where a card clicked again comes back.

entries.name: Cards the opponent looks at
entries.rule: They come off the top of their library face down at library size and lie beside it; a top-bound card slides back onto the library and a bottom-bound one slides away from it, to either side. A pill above their avatar reads "Scry: 1 top, 1 bottom." for about 3 s.

arena.does: No card is enlarged.

entries.name: Choosing from a list
entries.rule: The entries stand in a column over the shaded table. A press lights an entry and "Submit 1" answers with it, where Arena takes a color at the press: no card asks for an entry yet, and the prompt is the one a longer list needs, a creature type or a card name.

arena.does: Mother of Runes' color: Choose One over Choose Color, and White, Blue, Black, Red and Green in a column, each taken at a click.

entries.name: Choosing how to cast
entries.rule: A card or permanent with more than one way to cast or use it opens a modal, "Choose One", showing the card once per option, with Cancel: an adventure, an alternative cost, a land's abilities. A permanent with two or more activated abilities that are not mana abilities, as a planeswalker, opens it on every click, with each of those abilities in the card's order: one it cannot activate now, as a loyalty ability its loyalty cannot pay, is shown dimmed and takes no press.

arena.does: Brazen Borrower, Bonecrusher Giant and Force of Will open it from hand, Wasteland on the battlefield. Liliana of the Veil at 3 loyalty opens it with all three loyalty abilities, the +1 and −2 outlined and the −6 without the outline, dimmed.

entries.name: Choosing X
entries.rule: The value of X is set by a step down and a step up beside it, over the button that answers, which says the value under its label: "Pay" over "X = 1". Beside the value stands the whole cost it makes, and the permanents that would pay it are outlined as the value changes. Beryl has the single steps alone.

arena.does: Mind Twist's X stands under the spell between -5, - and +, +5, on a button that reads Pay over X = 0, with Cancel.

entries.name: Dividing among targets
entries.rule: Each target wears its share on its card, between a step that raises it and a step that lowers it, under the arrow to it; "Submit" answers once everything is given out. The prompt says after what it asks how much is still to give, as a cost paid with permanents says what is left.

arena.does: Fire Covenant's damage: an arrow from the spell to each target, a count on each between an arrow up and an arrow down, Submit and Cancel.

entries.name: Hover inspection
entries.rule: A hovered card in hand rises upright and grows in place, with no inspector beside it: about 0.3 of the table's height wide, its foot on the bottom edge, less where it would cover a card a prompt asks you to pick. It may cover your own life orb. It eases up in a tenth of a second and back down into the fan in about a sixth when the pointer leaves. A hovered permanent gets a separate copy about three times its size, away from the cursor, with its keywords explained. A card on the stack gets none. A card a prompt holds up in its tray, such as a card put back from the hand, is already shown large: hovered, it only turns upright and lifts a little in its place, and dragged, it keeps its size and faces the camera.

arena.does: The raised hand card is 0.29 to 0.31 of the table's height wide (1.8 times a card at rest in its hand), its top 0.58 of the way down, its foot just inside the bottom edge, over the avatar where it lies there, and no preview shows beside it; the permanent's copy is estimated from stills. The hand card's rise (70 to 130 ms) and drop (130 to 200 ms) were filmed at 30 frames a second; each covers about half its way in the first frame and slows as it arrives. In the "Order Cards" screen a hovered card turns upright and rises about 0.015 of the table's height within a frame, about its size at rest, and a dragged card stays upright at about its size there while its neighbors make room.

entries.name: Mana into what it pays for
entries.rule: Each tapped land glows and sends one streak of its color straight to the spell on the stack, which flashes as they land, in about 0.3 s. Mana does not stop at a pool.

arena.does: Seen for casts paid with lands.

entries.name: Ordering cards on a library
entries.rule: Cards a player puts back on their library in an order of their choice (Halimar Depths, and the cards a look leaves on top or on the bottom) lie in one row under "Order Cards", the library's top card at the right: "Bottom" is written under the row's left end and "Top" under its right. A card dragged along the row goes where it is let go. A scry keeps its two piles, and cards put back from the hand keep their own screen (exception 8).

arena.does: Ponder's "Order Cards", over "Drag cards to order them on top of your library.", has the three cards in a row with Bottom under its left end and Top under its right; Brainstorm's has the same ends.

entries.name: Passing to the end step
entries.rule: "End Turn" passes until the end step, or the player's next stop where the end step is not one, through every spell and ability the opponent puts on the stack meanwhile. It stops sooner only for a decision other than priority, such as declaring blockers; "Resolve" beside it is the way to stop at the opponent's next spell.

arena.does: The button reads "End Turn" over "To End", and goes blank while it passes.

entries.name: Permanents that leave
entries.rule: A permanent that is not a token dissolves where it is: destroyed, it breaks into ash at its slot; exiled, it becomes a vortex there. Nothing flies to the pile. What it leaves room for closes up only once it has gone.

arena.does: A destroyed creature glows and falls to ash over about 1 s; the spell then goes to its graveyard. The row closes up after the permanent is gone.

entries.name: Targeting a spell
entries.rule: With one spell on the stack, a spell that targets a spell takes it with no prompt and no Confirm. With more, a "Choose One" browser of the stack, "Target a spell.", opens with nothing preselected, Submit and Cancel.

arena.does: Counterspell and Mana Leak at a lone spell go straight onto the stack; Spell Pierce over two spells opens the browser at "Submit 0".

entries.name: The hand's fan
entries.rule: Your hand's cards lie along one circle over the near edge, about 14 card widths across, on the desktop and the phone. A card's turn and how far it sinks follow its distance from the fan's middle, so a crowded hand lies nearly flat and a spread one curves, and no card turns or drops further than its neighbors. the client shows the printed cost on the card face. Inspecting a card reveals its printed cost when a neighbor covers it.

arena.does: Measured from whole-table frames: a card's turn grows by about 0.0275° for each pixel it lies from the middle, with cards 180 pixels wide on a table 1920 wide, at 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 18 cards. Its outer cards turn about 11° at 8 cards and 14° to 15° at 10 and 18. Cards sit about one card's width apart until the hand reaches the turn button, then close up. Each card's mana cost floats above its top right corner, over the card beside it, so that every cost shows at 10 cards.

entries.name: The kept opening hand
entries.rule: When the opening closes, the screen over the table goes at once, and the hand it showed drops from there into the hand at the near edge in about an eighth of a second, slowing as it lands. On the phone the cards drop from the opening's rows. Nothing appears in the hand from nowhere.

arena.does: Arena's opening screen vanishes in one frame, and the hand, still fanned in the middle of the screen, falls into the hand at the bottom, most of the way in two frames of 30 and at rest after four.

entries.name: The local player's scry
entries.rule: The table is shaded and "Scry" shows the cards face up over it, BOTTOM on the left and TOP on the right, and Done; surveil's has Graveyard and Library boxes instead. The cards are the library's own: they come up from it as the prompt opens, and on Done the shade lifts at once and they go back to it at its size, none shown large on its way to the top or the bottom. A pill reads "Scry: 1 top, 1 bottom."

arena.does: Seen for a scry of two and for surveil; no card changes face.

entries.name: The opponent's turn
entries.rule: Arena's "Opponent's Turn" label shows in the action button's place, and no spinner.

entries.name: Tokens
entries.rule: They appear at their slot; they do not fly out of their source.

arena.does: Arena's appears whole with a short glow, about 0.1 s after its ability leaves the stack; a batch appears as one group.

entries.name: Two items on the stack
entries.rule: The top one still gets its target arrow. Each item beneath peeks out to the left of the one over it by a quarter of its width (a fifth past five items, as far as the room left of the stack allows), so a spell leaving from under another is seen as it goes.

arena.does: A cyan arc runs from the top item to its target, even when that is the one card under it; the top card sits a little right of and below the one beneath, which shows about a third of its width beside it, and a countered spell crumbles in that strip.

entries.name: Wording
entries.rule: Arena's exactly, case and punctuation too: "All Attack", "Choose attackers." Every prompt's title and buttons are one table in the session (`engine/crates/beryl_session/src/prompt/wording.rs`), each entry beside the recording moments that show it. A browser's title is the line that asks: its sentence of rules text, or its heading where the line under it only says how to drag. A pick is confirmed by "Submit" and the number picked, an arrangement by "Done", a "may" by "Take Action" or "Decline".

entries.name: Ability menus on a manual table
entries.rule: With Ability menus on, a permanent's context menu lists its ability costs and the start of each ability under Assists. −X opens the number prompt. Choosing an ability places a marker on the stack. The marker shows the source card and the ability text on hover and resolves with a click.

entries.name: Assist label
entries.rule: State nudges put clickable tags on the affected cards and life total. Click a tag to apply its suggested action.

entries.name: Chrome
entries.rule: Round icon buttons; the log toggle top left; the bug button above undo with no gap kept for a missing button.

entries.name: Command list
entries.rule: The manual table's command list shows what it acts on and filters commands by label as you type. Results are grouped by what they act on and show their shortcuts. Up and Down move between results, Return runs the selected command, Option+Return captures a new shortcut. The list reports when another command loses the key. Escape closes the list, and Shortcuts in the settings menu offers Reset shortcuts. On a phone, the search button opens the list full screen with a Close button and without key hints. Typed table prompts open at the top so the keyboard leaves the field visible.

entries.name: Context menu
entries.rule: The manual table's context menu names the card or pile and whose it is. It lists commands as plain labeled rows with key hints, check marks for active switches and at most one submenu level. A command that needs a number opens a prompt when chosen. On a phone, a long press opens a bottom sheet with the full card above the actions. A short hold before moving starts a drag. Dropping on the lower half of a library puts the card on the bottom. Draw arrow waits for a tap on the destination. Submenus replace the rows and offer Back. Select opens a bar with the count, Actions and Done while taps toggle cards. Play face down is available on the card, and Bottom card makes the next drag from that pile take its bottom card.

entries.name: Creating tokens on a manual table
entries.rule: The token chooser uses the command list layout and offers the selected card's tokens first. Typing searches the card store by name. Custom token opens a form for the token's name, type line, colors, power, toughness and note. Shift while choosing a token creates it face down.

entries.name: Guided manual table start
entries.rule: The step banner shows each player's die in the roll for first and shows another round on a tie. The winner, the named player or the previous game's loser gets Play or Draw on the opening screen. Both seats see their own opening hands and can Keep or Mulligan at the same time. They can confirm bottom cards or choose Done with none selected. The table moves to the first untap after both seats finish.

entries.name: Library drop halves
entries.rule: While a dragged card is over a library, the pile shows Top and Bottom. The half under the pointer lights up. Dropping multiple cards opens the ordering tray before the cards are moved.

entries.name: Lobby
entries.rule: Host a table, Join a table and Solo table open a manual table lobby. Phones can join or play solo. Each player chooses a deck, can change its sideboard and sets their own assists. The host shares an invite code. Both players see the connection, deck counts and match score. The host sets starting life, starting hand size and who plays first, and can start when both decks are loaded and the guest is ready. The gear menu opens the lobby as read-only information and lets either player record a result or confirm a concession. Both players return to the lobby with their decks ready for sideboarding.

entries.name: Manual counters and untap flags
entries.rule: Named counters use the existing counter badges with shortened names. Add counter offers six common names above the text field. Player counters appear beside the mana pool. A permanent marked as skipping untap shows a lock in its corner.

entries.name: Manual table announcements
entries.rule: The stage uses its existing step banner for a manual shuffle, roll, phase, turn, rewind or game start. It reads Shuffled, Rolled 4 (d6), Heads, the phase name, the active player's name followed by 's turn, Rewound to 41, or Game 2. The banner fades on the stage's clock.

entries.name: Manual table connection
entries.rule: A dropped connection freezes input on both seats under the existing step banner, which names the other player. The guest redials automatically and the returning view appears at once. A table that the other player left offers Lobby. The start screen offers Resume table for saved hosted tables and for the last table the guest joined. Quitting keeps the guest’s join available, and leaving the table clears it. Join failures appear on the join form, and a version mismatch appears for both players.

entries.name: Manual table library flows
entries.rule: When Library flows is on, the player's library menu offers Scry and Surveil under Assists. These and Look at top cards ask for a count, then open the shared sorting tray. A known card's Assists menu offers the library instructions on its visible face with the printed count. The other player sees the lifted cards and their destinations. A hidden card's identity stays private unless the other player already knew it or the card goes to a public zone.

entries.name: Manual table log
entries.rule: The log shows numbered entries with their actors. Rewinding strikes the entries after the chosen line. Cmd+Z and the undo button undo the viewer's latest action. Cmd+Shift+D undoes the viewer's latest draw. When later entries block an undo, the log opens and highlights them. Either player can undo a batch from its line or rewind from any line.

entries.name: Manual table pile viewers
entries.rule: The existing pile browser can be searched, grouped by card type, and sorted by name or mana value. The other player sees how many cards are lifted from a library during a look. Closing a full library search offers Shuffle and Don't shuffle, with Shuffle highlighted.

entries.name: Manual table prompts
entries.rule: Numbers, text and power/toughness are entered in the lower-right action dock. The field starts selected, and numeric entries have a step down and a step up. A sign changes the current value where one exists. The button says what it will do, such as Draw 3. Return confirms and Escape cancels.

entries.name: Manual table prompts
entries.rule: A guided choice on the manual table uses the same sorting tray or list as an engine game. The seat answering it sees the cards or choices. Across the table a library sort lifts only a packet of cards, which returns when the tray closes.

entries.name: Manual table turn controls
entries.rule: The step track lights the current step beside the active player's life total. Clicking an icon sets the phase. Clicking the lit Untap or Draw icon on your turn also performs that action. Cleanup selects End step. The Next button names the following phase and advances to it, wrapping to Untap. The Next turn command passes the turn.

entries.name: Manual table: a click acts
entries.rule: Click to tap or untap a permanent, play a card, resolve a stack entry, draw from the library, or open a graveyard or exile viewer. Shift-click plays face down. Click a life total to edit it in the number prompt. Click a mana symbol or a player counter to add one, or right-click to remove one. On phones, the mana total beside the life orb opens a sheet. Tap a symbol or counter to add one, or its minus button to remove one. The press shows immediately. A refused action shakes what was clicked.

entries.name: Manual table: drawing and removing arrows
entries.rule: Right-drag from a card to a card or life total to draw an arrow. A selected source draws an arrow from each selected card. A hand card plays first. A command that asks for a target starts the same aim and a click chooses the target. Escape cancels the aim. Right-click a drawn arrow to remove it, or use Cmd+R to remove all the arrows you drew.

entries.name: Nothing overlaps
entries.rule: The hand, the stack and their indicators never cover a control or each other. No layer of a library, graveyard or exile pile covers a card in play, for either seat, however long a row grows. The opponent's piles keep the band above their back row to themselves.

entries.name: Proposal panel
entries.rule: Turn upkeep and combat show the suggested changes with one checkbox per line and a mark on each affected card. Apply commits the checked lines as one undoable batch. The panel shares the log column on desktop and has its own strip on the phone.

entries.name: Quitting from a manual table
entries.rule: On the desktop, the Quit shortcut asks whether to leave the table and quit Beryl. Cancel keeps the table open.

entries.name: Selection rectangle
entries.rule: On a manual table, dragging from empty felt selects the cards the rectangle touches. Selected cards wear the gold selection mark. A summary beside the selected permanents gives their count, total power and total toughness.

entries.name: Suggestions are sensible
entries.rule: The suggested untap targets and the auto-pay sources are the ones a player would pick.

entries.name: The opponent's choice of top or bottom
entries.rule: When the opponent puts a card on the top or the bottom of their library by their own choice (Subtlety's "their choice of the top or bottom"), a pill beside that library reads "Top" or "Bottom" as the card goes there, and fades as a scry's pill does. Your own choice gets none. Arena shows no words: the card only goes to the library (iRr-GeSF0lI 1:01:07.5).

entries.name: Undo
entries.rule: Every answer can be undone, across turns and prompts, the cast and its payment together.

entries.name: Why a click is refused
entries.rule: An illegal click shows its reason at the permanent that forbids it.

entries.name: A battlefield row that scrolls
entries.rule: A row with more cards than fit with a strip of each uncovered shows as many as fit, scrolls one group for each notch of the wheel or 48 points of a sideways drag, and shows the number of cards off each end, as "+12".

entries.name: A card picked face down
entries.rule: While the other player still has to pick, as for Show and Tell, a card a player has picked from their hand lies apart from that hand where the cards a player handles lie: face up for its player, face down for the other. On the phone it lies beside its owner's library, toward the table, as the cards the opponent looks at do. Arena's recordings show no such pick.

entries.name: A card turning face up
entries.rule: A face-down permanent turning face up enlarges in place and flips; one leaving reveals its face during its flight, and one that leaves for a hand or a library, where no face shows, joins the Revealed Cards as it goes. Nothing turns face up in the recordings, and one face-down card is seen leaving.

arena.does: Killed, Arena's face-down card dissolves as a card back and a "Revealed Cards" panel then shows its face at the top left.

entries.name: A copy on the stack
entries.rule: It appears on the stack with no flight. None is seen.

entries.name: A cost paid as a spell resolves
entries.rule: Mana streaks from its sources into the resolving spell or ability, as into a spell being cast. No such payment is seen.

entries.name: A creature that enters attacking
entries.rule: It gets an explicit choice of what it attacks, and its line stays drawn throughout.

entries.name: A free mulligan
entries.rule: In a shared-deck game, when a player's opening hand qualifies before a regular mulligan, the mode mulligan prompt adds a third button, "Free Mulligan", stacked with "Mulligan" above the primary "Keep 7" button. Taking it reveals the hand to the opponent in the Revealed Cards pile (showcase) before the hand goes back into the shared library with the mulligan's motion and a new seven-card hand is dealt.

entries.name: A hand in two rows
entries.rule: In the client, a hand with more cards than one fan across the window holds with a strip of each uncovered, such as 60 cards, is laid in two or more fans, one behind and above the other, in hand order from the back fan to the front. Each card keeps a strip to press, and raises under the pointer as in one fan. Arena's recordings show no hand that large.

entries.name: A linked exile returning
entries.rule: The exiled card returns as its source departs, moving with it. No exiling permanent is seen leaving with its card returning.

entries.name: A mulligan's hand
entries.rule: It goes from sight where it lies, every card of it, as a permanent that leaves does; then the next hand is dealt as an opening hand is. No mulligan is filmed.

entries.name: A permanent changing sides
entries.rule: It flies across the battlefield to its new controller's row.

arena.does: Seen only before and after its move

entries.name: A permanent's chosen value
entries.rule: A value chosen as a permanent entered (a color, a creature type, a card name) shows on the permanent on one line, as a manual card's note does. Its inspection panel says "Chosen:" and the value.

entries.name: A spell that ends the turn
entries.rule: When a resolving spell ends the turn, play goes on to the cleanup step with no banner of its own: the turn is cut short as any turn ends, and the spell goes to its owner's pile (a shared-deck game's shared exile pile) in the move it would make at any other time. Arena's recordings show no spell that ends the turn.

entries.name: A target that moves
entries.rule: An arrow or line ends before either of its ends moves, and an arrow is not drawn again at a card that changed zones while its spell or ability stays on the stack. No target is seen leaving in response.

entries.name: A token that leaves
entries.rule: It dissolves in place like any permanent. No token leaving the battlefield is seen.

entries.name: An ability with no source on the battlefield
entries.rule: It emerges from the pile its source lies in, and appears on the stack when it has no source. No trigger from a graveyard is seen.

entries.name: An Aura that takes control
entries.rule: No Aura that gains control of what it enchants is in the recordings. Control Magic resolves as any Aura does: it flies from the stack to the creature and settles behind it in the creature's row. Then the creature slides, with the Aura, straight to its new controller's creature row, as a permanent changing sides does (Coveted Jewel, 0VsYGs88NXA 27:39.5). When the Aura leaves, the creature slides back the same way, after the spell that removed the Aura has gone.

entries.name: Arranging a melded or merged permanent's cards
entries.rule: When a melded or merged permanent is put into its owner's graveyard or library, the owner picks its cards one at a time, the bottom one first, in the ordinary pick prompt: "Choose the bottom card." The last card left goes on top. The recordings show no such move.

entries.name: Banding
entries.rule: When an attacker can start or join a band, the choice uses the existing option buttons. Attacking bands carry no extra mark on the table. Assign Damage uses the number control to assign a share to each creature in turn.

entries.name: Cards a look returns
entries.rule: Cards a look puts back into a library fly straight to it. The opponent's look at the top of their library that is not a scry lifts nothing: while they choose, their library lies as it was; each card it takes drops from the library into the table, deepest half way, and rises into their hand; the rest are never seen to move (Arena's Stock Up, 3sEoP_s4DQE 46:04.0, 0VsYGs88NXA 1:13:06.3, WCknTZNbraE 1:22:28.2). Your own look's cards put back are not filmed.

entries.name: Cards leaving a graveyard
entries.rule: A card returned to the battlefield or to your hand flies there from its pile; one returned to the opponent's hand swings up to a readable apex beside the stack before gliding to their hand (jD7VqaT8VC8 46:23.2). Returning to the battlefield or to your own hand is not seen.

entries.name: Cards moving to and from the shared piles
entries.rule: A card drawn, milled, put back or looked at in a shared-deck game uses the `fly` and `lift` motions a per-player game uses, starting or ending at the shared pile. A draw rises off the shared library and comes down to where the drawing player's draw ends: the viewer's beside the stack, the opponent's into their hand. A milled card crosses the table from the shared library to the shared graveyard on the same rising path as a per-player mill. The cards a player looks at lie beside the shared library, toward the middle of the table and half a card toward that player.

entries.name: Cards under a merged permanent
entries.rule: The other cards of a merged permanent (mutate) peek out from under it, as cards a permanent holds in exile do. Clicking one opens them all to read.

entries.name: Casting while searching a library
entries.rule: When a library search offers a spell to cast, the candidate buttons offer the cast alongside the cards the search can find and Done. After the cast, the search continues.

entries.name: Choosing a companion before the game
entries.rule: Before the opening hands are drawn, a player whose deck fulfills a sideboard card's companion condition gets the sideboard catalog titled Choose Companion, listing each card they may reveal. Done reveals none. Arena reveals a companion without asking.

entries.name: Choosing a replacement effect
entries.rule: When a draw could be replaced by dredge, the player picks the card to dredge, or declines and draws, with the pick prompt Beryl uses for choosing up to a number of cards. The title reads Choose an effect to apply, and its Decline button lets the draw happen. No card on Arena has dredge.

entries.name: Choosing a sideboard card during a game
entries.rule: The catalog shows eligible card names to the player making the choice. Done leaves every card in the sideboard. The chosen card is revealed and appears in its owner's hand.

entries.name: Choosing the deck
entries.rule: The New Game screen lists the decks a game can be played with, "WU Control" and "Dandân", as radio rows above the opponents, and its subtitle names the chosen one. On a phone the two stand side by side in the row of the sound button. The Dandân deck is one library both players draw from, so Fair deal, which compares two players' opening hands, is hidden while it is chosen. Arena's play screen has no equivalent.

entries.name: Controlling another player
entries.rule: While the viewer controls the opponent's turn, each decision they make for the opponent says "For opponent" before what it asks; a priority says only that.

entries.name: Copies
entries.rule: A permanent that is a copy shows the copied card's face with a "Copy" label where a token shows "Token" (the phone, which shows neither label, shows the copied card's scan). Its inspection panel names the card it really is.

entries.name: Dealing a fair game
entries.rule: With Fair deal ticked, Start leaves the start screen up while the session judges candidate deals, which takes a few seconds. The start button is disabled and reads "Dealing…" until the new game's first view arrives, and then the game screen opens. Arena has no fair deal.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.rule: It flies to the creature it becomes attached to.

arena.does: The equip ability leaves the stack with a flash at the creature; the equipment's own move is not seen

entries.name: Evoke and cycling
entries.rule: A card with evoke, or a land with cycling, opens the same "Choose One" modal. No evoke is seen; Triomes cycle straight to the stack, but whether a land could still be played is not shown.

arena.does: Arena shows no chooser before these cycles.

entries.name: FPS monitor
entries.rule: Settings can show a read-only panel at the top left of the native client. It reports current FPS, the lowest frame rate implied by a frame gap in the last minute, the app’s target, the display link’s rate when available, and the graphics tier being drawn, Enhanced or Baseline, in the settings sheet’s words.

entries.name: Hand cards put on the bottom
entries.rule: The split prompt is headed "Put cards on the bottom." The player orders any cards they put on the bottom and can press Done with all their cards in hand.

arena.does: The opponent resolves the spell and draws cards. Their choice is hidden.

entries.name: Inspecting a face-down manual card
entries.rule: The table shows a card back. Pointing at the card opens a face preview only if the viewer knows the card's identity.

entries.name: Known cards in a library
entries.rule: A known top card shows face up on its library. Clicking a library opens its browser, headed "Library" (or "Opponent's Library") and "N Cards": every card in library order, top first, each known card face up at its place and the rest as backs. No known card in the opponent's library is seen.

arena.does: The player's own library stays a card back after their tutor puts a card on top, and after a look. Its "Library" browser ("9 Cards") lists the cards top first in a row, three unknown ones as backs and then the known ones face up.

entries.name: Mana spent from a pool
entries.rule: It streaks from its player's pool into the spell or ability it pays for, as from a land. No floating mana is seen.

entries.name: Milled cards
entries.rule: They fly from the library to the graveyard face up, one after another as draws do. None is held up large first. No mill is seen.

entries.name: Mutating over or under
entries.rule: As a mutating creature spell resolves, its controller is asked as a top-or-bottom choice is, under the spell's name: "Over or Under?" with OVER and UNDER. The recordings show only the opponent mutating, never the choice. A card under a merged permanent is in the merged zone and is not drawn on the table.

entries.name: Notes on manual cards
entries.rule: A card shows its table note on one line, with an ellipsis when it runs out of room. Its inspection panel shows the full note.

entries.name: Other numbers
entries.rule: A changed power and toughness, and mana left in a pool, count as a life total does. Neither is seen.

entries.name: Paying with permanents
entries.rule: Waterbend, convoke, crew. Start with no payment highlights. Hover over Auto Pay on desktop or long-press it on mobile to see which permanents Beryl would use. Click or tap the button to accept. To pay manually, click or tap each permanent you want to contribute. For a three-creature Convoke, pick A, B and D directly even if Auto Pay would use A, B and C. After each manual pick, recalculate the proposal for the remaining cost and keep the player's picks. Let the player finish manually or accept Auto Pay for the remainder, and stop taking picks once the cost is covered. A question whose yes pays a cost at once (pay {1}, or the spell is countered) shows what that button would tap the same way, on hover or a long press, and nothing before. Arena documents the preview and acceptance gestures in its [May 23, 2019 patch notes](https://devtrackers.gg/magic-arena/p/3e5941f1-may-23-0-15-00-00-patch-notes). A selected permanent turns and carries a tap mark, and an outline means one thing at a time: at rest every permanent that can pay wears the outline of what may be picked, and while Auto Pay shows its proposal those it would tap alone show, in their ring. Once a pick has paid part of the cost, the prompt says after what it asks how much is still to pay.

entries.name: Permanents entering together
entries.rule: When permanents a player controls enter the battlefield at the same time and the order of their timestamps could change what their abilities do, the player picks them one at a time, earliest first, in the ordinary pick prompt: "Choose which enters first." Arena orders them without asking, as far as the recordings show.

entries.name: Phased-out permanents
entries.rule: A phased-out permanent stays where it lay, faded. It is never offered as a candidate, and its inspection panel says "Phased out".

entries.name: Shared piles
entries.rule: A shared-deck table draws one shared library, one shared graveyard and one shared exile pile with the same card look, tilt and scale as per-player piles, placed from each profile's `shared_piles` data in one column at the table's left edge on every layout: the library on the seam between the two players' creature rows, the graveyard above it and the exile pile below it. The battlefield rows beside the column start right of it, and the phone's prompt pill and phase icon keep clear of it. The per-player pile places stay empty.

entries.name: Text-changed cards
entries.rule: A spell or permanent whose text or type line was changed by a text-changing effect shows a "Text changed" tag on the table, renders Beryl's card frame with its new type line and rules text on the table and in the zoom view, and renders any ability it puts on the stack with its changed text on the ability plate.

entries.name: The opponent's draws and discards
entries.rule: A card the opponent draws flies face down from their library to their hand, as long as any card flies and never spinning round on the way. One they discard flies to their graveyard and turns face up on the way, as their spells do. Only the player's own are seen.

entries.name: The phone
entries.rule: It plays what the desktop plays; its layout and gestures are Beryl's own. Every motion is one of the desktop's verbs between the phone's places. A card flies between your hand's fan, the stack in the middle band and its row; the opponent's leaves and joins the card backs at the top edge. A draw leaves the library's pile in its player's strip, and a card put into a graveyard lands on that pile. An ability lifts out of its source to the stack, and a token appears in its row. The rows make room as the middle band grows for the stack, so a source glides aside while its ability lifts. An exiled card rests unseen under its owner's graveyard and is listed in that graveyard's sheet under exile's name, while one held by a permanent remains tucked under it. An emblem stands after its controller's other permanents, and its ability lifts from that card. Crowded rows overlap rather than shrinking creature cards below 56px high. A hand too large for one row takes further rows above it, to the right of its player's piles, which stay in view. Its newest cards stand in those rows. The phone centers a board at most 430px wide and scales a 375px board to fit narrower screens. Sounds follow the same steps. What the desktop shows around its table is composed for the phone from the same pieces. On the phone's start screen, the opponent list scrolls between the sound and credits controls at the top and the seed, the Fair deal checkbox and the game buttons at the bottom. The game result shows over the board with its reason and any culprit card centered, and the full-width result buttons stay above the bottom safe area when the result is shown or put aside. The opening shows the coin above two centered rows of cards, with bottom picks in slots beneath the hand and full-width actions above the bottom safe area. The menu button opens the settings with the log and the bug report in them. Undo and full control's mark stand at the end of the middle band, across from the phase. Unspent mana lies beside its player's life total, and the combat damage on its way on the total's rim. A touch on a graveyard, or on a library with a known card, lists its cards; a touch on a card shows it whole, and a touch beside it puts it away. The turn's banner crosses the middle band, a combat step's lies under the opponent's strip, and a scry's pill beside its player's lands, past the end of their row; a coin is tossed just above the middle band. A prompt picked on the table is the desktop's: the button it puts forward stands in the player's strip where the turn button is, with the one that passes on beside it; what it asks is a pill on the middle band's line, as Arena writes it across the middle of the table, or at the nearest height clear of every card where the stack lies on that line, and over the strip while the table is shaded under cards the prompt holds up; its other buttons are stacked over the turn button. A touch on a card the prompt can use uses it, and one it has no use for shows the card whole; a card in your hand is read by a touch and played by carrying it out of the hand. The Revealed Cards lie in the opponent's strip beside their graveyard, at a pile's size with no pill, and a touch opens them as it opens a pile. The bug reporter freezes the whole page and saves both that frame and the region the player selects. On a phone, the reporter opens from the menu, a touch selects the whole screen or a drag selects a region, the description stays above the keyboard, and a saved report offers Share and Done. Android's Back closes the open sheet or bug reporter and otherwise leaves a game in place. The phone keeps dark system chrome in either system appearance. The bottom actions clear the gesture bar, and the seed and game buttons rise above the numeric keyboard.

entries.name: The Revealed Cards between reveals
entries.rule: The pile holds what one spell or ability revealed, and what another reveals takes its place; a card revealed and then put where its face shows (a graveyard, exile, the battlefield, the stack) is not held up, since its flight shows it. The pile opens into the viewer every pile opens into. The recordings show the pile with one effect's cards at a time, dismissed before the next.

arena.does: One spell's four revealed cards lie in the pile together; the next reveal seen comes after the pile was dismissed.

entries.name: Why a creature can't attack
entries.rule: During Choose attackers, clicking or tapping a creature you control that cannot attack plays the refusal sound and opens the inspector with the reason under its face: "Tapped", "Summoning sickness", "Defender needs <subtype>" (reflecting text-changing effects), or "Can't attack".

entries.name: Words: prompts Beryl folds
entries.rule: Where Arena asks before a choice, Beryl opens the choice (exception 3) and words it from both screens. One discard in place of several: "Discard a basic land card or {most:words} cards." A look that may take nothing is its sentence as a question, with "Decline": "Put {most:words} of them into your hand?", "Exile {most:words} of them?", "Put {most:words} of them into your library?", "Put {most:words} of them into your graveyard?", "Put {most:words} of them onto the battlefield?". The other way about, Arena opens a payment that may be declined and Beryl asks first: "Pay {cost}." is answered "Pay {cost}" or "Decline". A card offered to cast is cast by its button, "Cast".

arena.does: Arena asks Discard a basic land card? and then Discard two cards.; a look that may take nothing is headed Choose One over a question, with Submit and Decline; a payment that may be declined has Decline beside Auto Pay.

entries.name: Words: prompts the recordings lack
entries.rule: Each is composed from the nearest prompt Arena shows. A discard to hand size: "Discard {most} cards." A mulligan of more than one card: "Return {most} Cards". Manifest dread: "Manifest one of them." Cards put back from a hand: "Put a card on top.", "Put {most:words} cards on top." A fateseal: "Top of Library", answered "BOTTOM" or "TOP" as a scry's piles are named. A card that goes on top or bottom with no asker to name: "Top or Bottom?". Looked-at cards sent to a graveyard or the battlefield: "Put {most:words} of them into your graveyard.", "Put {most:words} of them onto the battlefield." One card a filter names, looked at and sent somewhere Arena's recordings do not show: "Put {what} into your hand.", "Put {what} into your hand?", "Exile {what}.", "Put {what} into your library.", "Put {what} into your library?", "Put {what} into your graveyard.", "Put {what} into your graveyard?", "Put {what} onto the battlefield." An optional move of a card anywhere but to exile: "Put that card into your hand{from}?", "Put that card into your graveyard{from}?", "Put that card onto the battlefield{from}?", "Put that card into your library{from}?", "Move that card{from}?". A cost of no mana: "Pay {0}." The opening choices: "Play or draw?", answered Play or Draw, and "Keep or mulligan?" over Arena's own buttons. Catalogs: "Choose Creature Type", "Choose Word to Replace", "Choose New Word". Waterbend: "Tap permanents to Waterbend". Convoke: "Tap creatures to Convoke". Improvise: "Tap artifacts to Improvise". What a declared creature is aimed at: "Choose attack target", "Choose what to block". Piles of a split: "Hand", "Exile", "Battlefield". The pass button's captions for where Arena shows none: "To Untap", "To Upkeep", "To Main 1", "To Main 2", "To Cleanup", "Nothing to play" under a halt and "To Opponent's Turn" under the player's own End Turn. The own-target warning (exception 7) asks Arena's question less its end, "Do you want to target {name}?", and a spell picked on the stack reads "Target {name}", or the warning's question where it is the player's own.

arena.does: Only the opponent's manifest dread, fateseal and put-back are seen, and games begin with the first player chosen.

entries.name: Words: what a card's text would say
entries.rule: Arena words many prompts from the text of the card that asks, which a prompt's record does not carry. A look, a search or an optional search whose cards a filter of the asking spell or ability chose names one of them as the card does, as Arena does: "Search for {what}.", "Search your library for {what}?", where {what} reads, for example, an artifact card with mana value 1 or less. Otherwise Beryl says what Arena says of any card, or the same sentence less the card's part: "Choose a target.", "Search for a card.", "Search your library?", "Exile a card.", "Exile {most:words} cards.", "Distribute damage.", "Distribute counters.", "Choose One" over a card chosen for an effect, and an optional effect under its asker's name ("{source}", or "Take Action?" with none). Braces are the table's holes.

arena.does: Arena names the card's own: Target a creature., Search for a basic land card., Exile a blue card., Draw a card?

entries.name: Your own spell returned to hand
entries.rule: It glides from the stack to the hand, turning as it goes. Only the opponent's spells are seen returned.

verbs.name: fly
verbs.shows: A card travels from where it is to its new place, and flashes as it lands on the battlefield, unless it is a land played from a hand: a land played, a spell cast, a permanent spell resolving, a draw, a discard, an aura onto its permanent. One whose face changes turns over on the way, top over bottom and seen in depth: a spell begins to tip away as it clears the hand, is edge-on about two fifths of the way along, leaning a little off level, lies flat with its face up about a sixth of a second after it began to tip, and flies the rest of its way face up, a drawn card turns over as it leaves the library and flies face up, and one that lay the other way up the table never spins round besides. A card you draw flies from the library across the table to a place beside the stack, where one drawn alone is held up large to be read, sinking a little, and then drops into the right end of the hand; each of several drawn together sweeps past that place without stopping and comes down into the hand, which has made room for them all as the first left. A card that comes to a hand joins its right end, and keeps its place there. The cards that stay in a hand as one joins or leaves it move to their new places in about a sixth of a second, slowing into them, as the change happens: as a drawn card leaves the library, and as a card cast or played leaves the hand. A card that lands face down the other way up the table, as the opponent's draw does, leaves the way up it will lie. A spell cast leaves the straight line in a shallow arc that bows toward its controller's edge of the table. A permanent resolving, either player's, is thrown up off the stack: it is smaller in its first frame, rises up the screen at once, crosses most of the way to its place at that height, half way across after a quarter of its time, and then drops onto its place, shrinking as it comes down. The player's own land glides straight to its place. The opponent's land leaves its slot face up, leans as it swings down and right past their life badge, then levels out and glides back into the land row. Its shadow separates during the swing and fades as the card settles. A permanent waits on the stack until the flare of the mana that paid for it has gone, and then leaves.

arena.does: A played land glides from where it is released to its slot in about 0.3 s, gathering speed, and lands with no flash. The opponent's land leaves their hand face up, leans as it moves down and right, and reaches about two thirds of the table's width and three tenths of its height after a quarter second. It levels out, and glides left and up into its slot about 0.6 s after it left, with no flash. The opponent's spell leaves their hand as a card back and is face up when it reaches the stack, about 0.4 s; the player's own flies from where it is released in about 0.35 s. A resolving permanent, either player's, is the smaller battlefield card one frame after it leaves the stack, rises up the screen by about a fifth of the table's height within 0.1 s, crosses to above its slot at that height and drops onto it, about 0.5 s in all, and the slot flashes. A drawn card leaves the library at the lower left leaning a little, turns face up within about 0.2 s at the size it had there, flies right across the table to a place beside the stack growing as it comes, holds there about 0.2 s and drops into the right end of the hand, about 1.1 s in all; three drawn by one spell leave a quarter second apart and fly the same way with no hold, about 0.7 s each. A discard drops to the graveyard at hand size in about 0.2 s.

verbs.name: appear
verbs.shows: A card comes to be at its place with no flight: a token, the opening hand, a card a look put in the graveyard, a permanent put into a library. Its row makes room in its delay, so it shows at a place already open.

arena.does: A token appears whole with a short glow, a batch as one group. The opening hand and a mulligan's new hand are there at once. A permanent put into a library is on the library face up within a frame, with nothing left where it was, and slips in 70 to 130 ms later.

verbs.name: vanish
verbs.shows: A card or an ability goes from where it is with no flight, and a card is at its new place as it is gone: destroyed, exiled, sacrificed, countered, returned to a hand, or done resolving. Its step is its going alone; what it left room for closes up after, as one move even where the going is a cut, and where nothing does the next thing follows at once.

arena.does: A destroyed permanent falls to ash in about 1 s, an exiled one becomes a vortex, a sacrificed one flashes, and a returned one glows and is gone; none flies to a pile or a hand. A countered spell crumbles on the stack. A resolved instant darkens and dissolves there, or shrinks into its graveyard. A finished ability is gone between two frames.

verbs.name: emerge
verbs.shows: An ability lifts out of its source and goes on the stack: a small copy appears in the middle of its source and travels all but straight to the stack, sagging a little toward the middle of the table, and grows as it goes. The source stays as it is. A triggered ability shoots a beam of light toward the middle of the table about 0.1 s after it comes to rest, and the line to its source appears whole once the beam has gone.

arena.does: A small copy of the card appears in the middle of the source, about a quarter of its size on the stack, and travels to the stack, growing evenly with the way it has come, in 0.25 to 0.35 s; an activated ability does the same. Filmed whole, the way is all but straight: it sags at most 0.025 of its length, toward the middle of the table, from either seat. A triggered ability flares white at the stack about 0.1 s after it comes to rest, for about 0.27 s, while gold sparks hang along the way it came. Two triggers of one event leave 0.3 s apart. A dies trigger leaves before its source breaks up.

verbs.name: flip
verbs.shows: A card turns over where it lies: a double-faced card transforms, a face-down permanent turns face up (not seen: built as "A card turning face up" says).

arena.does: A transforming card is covered by an effect (a lava slab, a cocoon) for about 1.1 s and shows its new face as the effect clears; it neither turns nor grows.

verbs.name: tap
verbs.shows: A permanent turns a quarter as it taps or untaps, its whole card about its own middle where it lies. Its row then closes up or makes room, the tapped apart from the untapped.

arena.does: Arena tilts a tapped permanent's art crop 7 to 8 degrees in about 0.2 s and dims it; an untap restores it in about 0.1 s.

verbs.name: strike
verbs.shows: A creature rears back, grows a little toward the eye and leans toward the side of what it deals combat damage to, hangs there a moment, then dashes onto it in a few frames; what it strikes flashes and the whole table shakes as the blow lands; it stays on it a moment and drifts back, leaning less as it goes. A player's life total changes on that blow. Two creatures that strike each other meet half way, at one time. A strike that would pass over a creature of an earlier strike still on its way out or back waits until that one is home. On something much smaller than itself it lands whole, shrinking as it goes.

arena.does: Each attacker rears back about half a card and leans about 15 degrees in about 0.1 s, hangs there about 0.3 s, dashes onto the player's avatar or its blocker in about 0.07 s, the table shakes for about 0.17 s, and it stays a moment and drifts back, 1.2 to 1.4 s in all. A blocked attacker strikes about 0.4 s before an unblocked one. First strike is a strike of its own, seconds earlier.

verbs.name: streak
verbs.shows: A streak of light leaves one thing and lands on another, which flashes: mana from its source into the spell or ability it pays for, and damage from a spell or ability to what it hits. It rises out of its source's row toward the middle of the table on a low arc, a bright head with a tail behind it, gathering as it leaves and quickening all the way, and its tail is drawn in as it lands. Mana leaves as its source begins to turn, several into one spell together, and has left the row before the row closes up; the mana of a pile of lands fans out to either side. A source with no place left on the table sends none: what its mana pays for only flashes.

arena.does: Each tapped land sends one streak of its color to the spell on the stack in about 0.3 s. A burn spell or ability glows, and a streak of fire crosses to its target in about 0.25 s, with a burst where it lands; the spell leaves after.

verbs.name: count
verbs.shows: A number changes and shows that it did: a life total, a kind of counter, a power and toughness, a mana pool.

arena.does: A life total jumps to its new value in a burst of about 0.4 s; a loss's red number drifts down from the opponent's avatar, and a gain's green one rises for about 0.5 s. A counter's badge settles onto its permanent after a flash. A planeswalker's loyalty changes about a second after its ability reaches the stack.

verbs.name: set
verbs.shows: The table changes and nothing moves: a step of the turn begins, a library is shuffled, a permanent's characteristics change.

arena.does: Nothing animates as a step begins, and nothing shows on a library when it is shuffled.

verbs.name: showcase
verbs.shows: A card an effect reveals is held up for both players to read: its face joins the "Revealed Cards" pile at the top left, growing into its place there, and the card itself lies where it was.

arena.does: Revealed cards gather under a "Revealed Cards" pill at the top left, each growing into place in about 0.2 s. A click on the pile opens a browser of them under the same words, with a Done button, and the pile stays afterward until the cross on its pill puts it away.

verbs.name: dwell
verbs.shows: Nothing moves while something is read: the opponent's spell or ability, before it resolves unanswered, and the table as the game ends, before the result covers it.

arena.does: The opponent's spell sits on the stack for 0.7 to 1.9 s before it resolves. After the play that ends a game the table stays in view about 3 s, the loser's avatar bursting for the first half of it, before the result covers it.

verbs.name: announce
verbs.shows: A notice passes over the table: the turn banner, the pill that says what a scry did, the pill beside a library that names the end of it the opponent chose for a card, a coin tossed. Play goes on under the banner and the pill, which are drawn over the cards in flight and fade in, stand and fade out, the banner sinking toward its player as it goes. A coin is waited for, and has the table to itself: it is thrown only once the turn's banner has gone, mid-table, rises a diameter and a half toward the viewer turning fast, falls back onto its plate quickening, lands with a swell and a flare, and only then says who won, which stands for the rest of its step.

arena.does: "Your Turn" or "Opponent's Turn" glows at the centre for about a second while cards move under it. A pill above an avatar reads "Scry: 1 top, 1 bottom." for about 3 s. A coin a card flips is tossed mid-table and lands in about 1.2 s.

verbs.name: point
verbs.shows: An arrow or line between two things, from the step that begins it to the step that ends it: to a target, from an ability to its source, from an attacker to the planeswalker it attacks, from a blocker to its attacker. An attacker at a player has no line, only its wedge. Each is drawn as light, a ribbon with a hot core. An arrow at a target is a bowed arc, a thread at its spell that swells to a spear head, whole in the frame it begins once its spell or ability has landed on the stack, which lands with a flash and sparks and has light run along it toward its target while it stands. It comes onto a card from the open table in front of it, never along its row, and its head lies on the card's face; at a player it goes over the top onto their life total; between two things that all but touch it goes round their side. One at the stack item its own lies over leaves the side of its own item and comes round into the end of the other's strip, its head on the table beside the stack, pointing at that item's name. The line to a source has no head and appears whole in a frame, about 0.45 s after its ability leaves its source: it leaves the bottom of the source as a hairline, hangs low over the table, where it is widest, and comes up toward the bottom of its ability, fading out before it reaches it, from either seat. It hangs to about 0.9 of the table's height between ends far apart across it, and only a little below the lower end between ends close together across it, about a third as far below it as they lie apart (by-olby); to a source that lies right under its ability it goes down from the bottom of the ability into the top of the source, and to one above it whose hanging line would cross the ability (a planeswalker on the opponent's row over the stack) it goes up from the top of the ability into the bottom of the source, never over the ability's face (by-52mf); a phone's arcs across between them. A line of combat is a straight beam that narrows to a dart, from the middle of its creature to the middle of what it points at, over both. Each is one line for as long as it lasts, drawn every moment from where its two ends are, and each is cut whole in a frame as the step that ends it ends, never drained away from its tail, which left a stub of arrow on its target (by-2e5a), which waits until it has stood whole for its end's delay, so that one whose spell resolves at once is still read, and which what follows waits for, so that neither end moves under it. An ability and the line to its source stay a moment after what the ability did, and go in one tick. Every arrow and line is over everything at rest and under what flies. A browser with no WebGL draws each as a path instead.

arena.does: A cyan arc runs from a spell or ability to its target until it resolves. A thin line joins an ability to its source from the frame it lifts. A thin gold line runs from a blocker to its attacker until combat damage is done. An attacker has no line to the player, only its chevron.

verbs.name: mark
verbs.shows: A mark from the list below on a card, an ability or a player, from the step that begins it to the step that ends it. The light of what may be picked comes up over a moment, on all of it at once. Every other mark is there in the tick its step begins, so that one which takes another's place on a card swaps with it, and each is gone as the step that ends it begins.

verbs.name: lift
verbs.shows: Cards the opponent is handling come away from their pile, face down, from the step that begins the look to the step that ends it. Cards the player's own prompt holds up come away from where they lie into its tray, face up, as the prompt opens; lie as each click sorts them; and go back to where the table has them as the first steps of what the answer did begin.

arena.does: Cards the opponent scries come off their library face down at its size and lie beside it.

effects.name: glow
effects.shows: A halo of warm light around a card, bright at once, that spreads and fades: the card is new here, is leaving whole, or sends a streak. On the stack, where the spell that acts on a card lies over it, the light is a rim inside the card's own frame.

effects.name: settle
effects.shows: A permanent that lands is whole for two frames, then whitens over its whole face, bursts in a round bloom of white light with thin rays about one and a half cards wide, throws a soft ring to twice its width and flecks that drift off, and stands washed white until the light is gone.

effects.name: dissolve
effects.shows: A card darkens, holds dark, and then breaks up along a stippled edge from the top down, for as long as its step: it is destroyed, countered or sacrificed.

effects.name: dim
effects.shows: A card darkens whole and fades where it lies, for as long as its step: a spell that has resolved is done.

effects.name: blanch
effects.shows: A card is lost in white light, for as long as its step: it is going to exile.

effects.name: cover
effects.shows: A veil of light closes over a card, hides it while it changes, and clears from what it now is, for as long as its step.

effects.name: impact
effects.shows: A burst of hot light on what a creature strikes or a streak of damage hits, a card or a player's life total: white-hot with rays and about one and a half of its widths across as the blow lands, spreading a little as it fades in about a third of a second, a ring leaving it.

effects.name: shake
effects.shows: The whole table jolts side to side and a little up and down, twice, each swing smaller than the last, as a creature's blow lands.

effects.name: trail
effects.shows: A streak of white light behind a creature as it dashes at what it strikes, widest at the card and thinning behind it, about as long as the card goes in a few frames, gone as the blow lands.

effects.name: flash
effects.shows: A flare of white light with rays over a spell or ability as the mana that pays for it lands, brightest at once, that spreads to about twice the card's width and is gone.

effects.name: beam
effects.shows: A cone of white and yellow light shoots from the side of a triggered ability that has come to rest on the stack, toward the middle of the table, from a little above its middle: it reaches nearly two cards' widths in a quarter of its time, narrows to a streak and fades, with a bloom on the card's edge where it leaves and gold sparks hanging along the way behind it.

effects.name: pulse
effects.shows: A ring of light round a card's frame while its numbers swell and settle: a counter put on it or taken off, its loyalty, its power and toughness.

effects.name: loss
effects.shows: A life total flares red, and the number that says how much it lost sinks away from it and fades, for as long as its step.

effects.name: gain
effects.shows: A life total flares green, and the number that says how much it gained rises from it and fades, for as long as its step.

marks.name: eligible
marks.means: The player may pick or use it now: a card to play, a permanent with an ability, a legal target, an attacker or blocker to declare, an option.

arena.does: Arena outlines all of these in one cyan, and neither dims nor outlines what cannot be picked.

marks.name: selected
marks.means: The player has picked it in the open prompt.

arena.does: A clicked attacker and a chosen blocker turn gold.

marks.name: suggested
marks.means: The offered default would use it: a permanent Auto Pay would tap, the blocker the session would deal lethal damage to next.
marks.look: An ember ring. Not seen in Arena.

marks.name: paying
marks.look: The permanent turns and carries a tap mark, with no outline. Not seen in Arena.

marks.name: hostile-target
marks.means: A target its chooser does not control.
